title: Proactive staleness honeypot and rollback orchestrator for verified performance profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) can drift as models, kernels, and infra change. Current refresh is manual-heavy and often discovers regressions after customers have been routed to new pins. We need an automated detector + orchestrator that proactively finds staleness, raises a verified alert, and can safely unpin or rollback a profile across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments without user-visible downtime.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight periodic "staleness honeypot" runner that: (1) executes a minimal, representative micro-benchmark set (golden prompt suite) against the pinned model+runtime combo; (2) compares latency/cost/throughput signatures to the canonical profile with time-series and statistical tests; (3) if drift exceeds configurable thresholds, escalate to an automated rollback orchestrator that (a) places the profile into a quarantined state, (b) optionally routes small percentages of traffic away (canary diversion) and resumes additional sampled runs, and (c) if confirmed, triggers an automated rollback plan (unpin to last known-good or pin to a fallback variant). The system will emit signed audit artifacts (profile status, sample telemetry, attestation) and require operator approval for irreversible changes for Private customers.

Scope: Profile verification automation, honeypot runner, statistical drift detection, rollback orchestration, signed audit trail, console UI flags for quarantined profiles, and runbook updates. Not included: model retraining, full production shadowing of user PII traffic (we will use synthetic/golden prompts and sampled non-PII traces).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Honeypot runner executes scheduled micro-benchmarks for all published verified profiles at configurable cadence (default daily) and stores results in profile-audit index.

A2: Drift detection runs a defined statistical test (e.g., median latency change + 95th percentile tail test) and flags profiles when thresholds exceeded (default: latency +20% median OR P95 +30% OR cost delta +15% OR throughput drop >25%).
A3: Quarantine workflow moves flagged profiles into 'quarantined' state in the catalog and marks them as not eligible for new autoscale allocations; console shows quarantine badge and reason.

A4: Rollback orchestrator can automatically unpin and repoint pinned routes to the previous signed profile variant in <5 minutes for Hosted/Dedicated, with non-destructive audit logs and signed attestations using KMS key.
A5: For Private deployments, the system creates a rollback proposal requiring operator approval; proposal includes sample traces, delta metrics, and a one-click rollback action in Console.
A6: Integration tests exercise the end-to-end flow (honeypot -> flag -> propose rollback -> execute rollback) using synthetic traces and a test runtime; telemetry assertions present in CI.
A7: Runbook and incident template documented in Confluence and linked from Console; on-call team notified according to existing SLO playbooks.
decision_log: D1: Use synthetic 'golden prompts' + sampled non-PII production traces rather than full shadowing to balance signal vs. privacy and cost.
D2: Default drift thresholds established iteratively; starting thresholds set to capture major regressions while limiting false positives (see A2).
D3: Automatic rollback allowed for Hosted/Dedicated but not for Private by default; Private requires operator sign-off due to customer controls.
D4: Audit artifacts will be signed with the platform KMS key and persisted to the profile ledger for post-mortem and compliance requests.
implementation_notes: IN1: Honeypot runner should be a small serverless job (Fargate or Cloud Run) that calls the same runtime entrypoints used by customers to avoid instrumentation differences.
IN2: Use deterministic golden prompts stored in the performance-profile Git-backed manifest; manifest versioning ensures reproducibility of checks.
IN3: Drift detection pipeline implemented in runtime-metrics-job with short windowed aggregations (1h, 24h) and baseline comparison to the profile's canonical fingerprint.
IN4: Rollback orchestrator will leverage existing rollout controller APIs (canary/diversion) and extend them with a 'quarantine' state and emergency-unpin operation.
IN5: Signed attestations will include hash of the profile manifest, timestamp, run outputs, and KMS signature; store references in the profile ledger (S3 + GCS index).
IN6: Monitor cost impact of running honeypots; optimize by running more frequently for high-traffic profiles and less often for longtail low-usage profiles.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge design doc and security sign-off (2d).
Step 1: Implement honeypot runner and manifest hooks; unit tests + local e2e harness (1 sprint).
Step 2: Implement drift-detector with threshold config stored in profile metadata; deploy to staging, run 48h against staging catalog (1 sprint).
Step 3: Add quarantine state and Console UI flags; user experience review with PM/Design (0.5 sprint).
Step 4: Implement rollback orchestrator for Hosted/Dedicated and add Private proposal workflow; protect with feature flag (1 sprint).
Step 5: Integrate KMS signing for audit artifacts and add persistence to ledger; security review & key rotation checklist (0.5 sprint).
Step 6: Small-scale beta with internal teams and 3 pilot customers; adjust thresholds and false-positive heuristics (2 weeks).
Step 7: Public launch with documentation, runbook, and telemetry dashboards; post-launch monitoring window 4 weeks.
